also a rogue; कुळंकषा (a river) sweeping away its banks; झाळंकषः dashing against, coming in collision with the clouds as the wind; करीषकषा blowing away dry cowdung, as a strong wind or gale. भय is added to एषु cau. as in जनमेषयः making the people tremble with fear; name of a king;—to अस्, ते, तुद् and ह्व 'to go' after the words वात, क्षुधि, तिला and छार्दै flatulence; वातभयः facing the wind, a kind of deer; क्षुधिभयः: a kitten; तिलेभुदः an oilman; and छर्द्जंहाः causing flatulence (भायाः) a kind of bean;—to ये and ध्मा after the words स्तन and नाडी, respectively. स्तनंययः a baby sucking breast; नाडि-(डी)ध्मः: a goldsmith;—to तुद् after विधु and अरुष; विधुतुदः: the afflictor of the moon i. e. Rāhu; अरुतुदः: (अरूंषि मर्माणि तुदतीति) wounding the vital parts, painful;—to पच् after words showing measure as प्रस्थेपचा स्थाली, खारिपचः कटाहः and after मित and नख-मितपचः: one who cooks measured corn, a miser; नखपचा nail-scorching (as यवाराः);—to हर् and तप् after the words अहर्य and छलाट; अहर्यहराः: those who do not see the sun i. e. the queens of a king who are shut up in the harem; छलाटतपः scorching the forehead;—to इष्, मद् and धमा afer उर, रुद्र and पाणि respectively; उर्मेषय of a fierce aspect, इरद्मदः lightning; पाणिधमः: a road (shrouded in such darkness that one has to clap one's hands for driving away serpents &c. that may be in the way); to मन् meaning 'to consider oneself' as, पण्डितमन्य, a pedant, who considers himself a Pandita; गोमन्यः: one who considers himself a cow i. e. who is very humble; &c.

र—is added to any root with ईषत्, दुर् or सु prefixed to it when the idea of ease or difficulty is present, ईषत्करः done easily; दुष्कर done with difficulty; सुकर done easily; so दुःशासन, दुर्योधन, &c. &c.

र—is added in the sense of the place or the instrument of the action or forms abstract nouns; कृ with आ-आकरः a mine; खन् with आ, आखनः a spade; पण with आ, आपणः a place of traffic; कष—निकषः a touch-stone; चर—गोचरः a pasture-ground; संचरः a path; वह—वहः a shoulder; निमेषः that by which the
